page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The business trip
title: The business trip
description:
Anna and Tom are on a very important business trip to try and sign a deal to sell their plastic fruit to a company in France. The company has received a better offer so Anna needs to clinch the deal and convince them that Tip Top Trading's lemons are best!
This episode focuses on what to say when you need to finish a deal.
phrases: Thank you for sparing the time to see us.
Each lemon comes with a satisfaction guarantee - I know you won't be disappointed.
I would be grateful if you could just sign the contract.
Thank you. It was a pleasure doing business with you.

listening_challenge.question: What does Tom offer to throw in as part of the deal with the company in France?
listening_challenge.answer: A free sample of the new Perfect Peach range.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom, could you let go of my hand?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Sorry, it's just I get nervous flying.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, we've landed in Marseille now so you're safe… oh, I like your passport photo.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh do you?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I didn't know your middle name was Stanley.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: After my great-great-grandfather.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Really? Come on we need to get a taxi. Taxi! Taxi!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again. Anna and Tom are on a very important business trip to try and sign a deal to sell their plastic fruit to a company in France. The company has received a better offer so Anna needs to convince them that Tip Top Trading's lemons are best. Are you feeling confident Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Not really. It was OK speaking to them on the phone but seeing them face-to-face is quite scary.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You'll be fine. Stay calm. They'll be pleased you've taken the time to fly out and see them – but tell them you're grateful for their time and recap what you told them on the phone.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh yes – beat the price of the competitor but get them to make a bigger order.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes. If they order more you can offer a bigger discount. Good luck.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh look, we're here now. Now Anna, I hope you don't mind me saying, but just leave the talking to me. Right?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err, well…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh, Madame Brown, ciao, great to see you

transcript.speaker: Trader
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Monsieur Brown. Bonjour. I'm Anna from Tip Top Trading. This is my colleague Tom. Thank you for sparing the time to see us.

transcript.speaker: Trader
transcript.text: No problem. Did you have a good flight?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It was great. I love those little bottles of wine they give out… I kept a few with me if you fancy a glass of vin rouge?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I think we should sit down and discuss business.

transcript.speaker: Trader
transcript.text: Of course.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah, good idea.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Now, I believe Tutti Fruity has offered you a good price but as I said on the phone, we can beat that.

transcript.speaker: Trader
transcript.text: Yes you did.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Did you Anna?!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But to get this price you've got to buy lots more.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna! That's not very subtle. You need to convince them they need to buy more without telling them they have to.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What she means is our Imperial Lemons are made with our unique laser curve technology. They are hard wearing and a joy to have on display in any shop window or restaurant.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom, that's amazing!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I read it on the back of the box!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: So, we really feel that we have a product that you'll be proud to display. And to get this fantastic price you just need to place an order of 10,000.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: And we can even throw in a free sample of our new Perfect Peach range.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Each lemon comes with a satisfaction guarantee. I know you won't be disappointed.

transcript.speaker: Trader
transcript.text: Hmm. It sounds good. OK, I think you have a deal.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Good work Anna. Don't forget to ask him to sign the contract and tell him when he can expect the order to be delivered.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK. I would be grateful if you could just sign the contract. We'll get the lemons to you as quickly as we can. Tom, do you have a pen?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Erm, no actually. It was in my bag yesterday but it's gone… it was a nice, a good one too.

transcript.speaker: Trader
transcript.text: No problem. I have a pen. There you go.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you. It was a pleasure doing business with you. We'll get those lemons to you in two weeks' time.

transcript.speaker: Trader
transcript.text: Perfect!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Good work Anna…oh and Tom too. The contract is signed but now you have to deliver what you've promised. There are many ways to clinch a deal; here are some of the phrases Anna used…

transcript.speaker: Thank you for sparing the time to see us.
transcript.text:
Each lemon comes with a satisfaction guarantee - I know you won't be disappointed.
I would be grateful if you could just sign the contract.
Thank you. It was a pleasure doing business with you.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So it's been a successful day. It's time for Tom and Anna to fly back to London and tell Paul the good news… or is it?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh no look, our flight to London is cancelled! It's the last one today. What are we going to do?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Well, I guess we're just going to have to stay here for the night. I'll sort out a hotel.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Until next time. Bye!
